mt-3.title: Task objectives scaled to fourteen targets
mt-3.note: Replaces the single target slot with a fourteen-target assignment. The paired objectives (high hit rate and zero-shot affinity) remain identical to the single-target brief.

mt-5.title: Fourteen-target specification table
mt-5.note: Replaces the single-target dossier paragraph with a structured five-column table (name, UniProt accession, organism, oligomeric state, notes). This establishes minimum metadata requirements before computational design begins.

mt-7.title: Target 1: EGFR ectodomain
mt-7.note: Monomeric receptor ectodomain with the most public binder-design precedent of any target here: two full Adaptyv competition rounds plus a preprint are in the reference list.

mt-8.title: Target 2: PD-L1
mt-8.note: Monomeric immune checkpoint ligand. Well-characterised interface with a clear mechanism of action for a blocking binder.

mt-10.title: Target 4: BBF-14, a synthetic control
mt-10.note: The only non-natural target: a de novo 8-stranded beta-barrel with no UniProt entry, identified by reference PDB and synthetic NCBI taxid. It functions as a negative control target lacking evolutionary history, paralogs, or literature binders.

mt-11.title: Target 5: BHRF1, a viral Bcl-2 homolog
mt-11.note: Epstein-Barr virus protein. Monomeric, and one of three viral or bacterial targets that break the human-protein assumption baked into most MSA and structure tooling.

mt-12.title: Target 6: MBP, with a disambiguation warning
mt-12.note: E. coli maltose-binding protein. The clarification 'NOT human myelin basic protein' prevents confusing two proteins sharing the MBP abbreviation, which would invalidate the target run.

mt-13.title: Target 7: SpCas9, whose functional unit is an RNP
mt-13.note: Nominally a monomer, but the note specifies the functional unit is a 1:1 Cas9:sgRNA ribonucleoprotein. That makes it the target most likely to trip the cofactor-representation rule: an arm that cannot accept nucleic acid input cannot represent this system, and the prompt forbids waiving the requirement on that basis.

mt-14.title: Target 8: TREM2 ectodomain
mt-14.note: Monomeric immunoreceptor Ig-like V-type domain, with prior competition data in the reference list.

mt-16.title: Target 10: TNFα, a C3 homotrimer
mt-16.note: The only three-fold-symmetric target. It drives the 1:N and N:N scoring requirement at its most expensive: three protomers means three binder copies in the N:N construct.

mt-17.title: Target 11: VEGF-A, an antiparallel disulfide-linked dimer
mt-17.note: C2 homodimer. The 'antiparallel' note matters for symmetry-operator construction of the N:N reference complex.

mt-18.title: Target 12: GDF-8, the only counter-screened target
mt-18.note: Homodimer, and the sole target carrying a COUNTER-TARGET. Designs must be selective against GDF-11, a close paralog, which activates a chain of otherwise-dormant clauses: a GDF-11 arm at the validation gate, selectivity-directed optimization, and the nine-term ranking formula with per-arm selectivity_delta. In the single-target release this same requirement is what distinguishes the two GDF-8 prompts from the other fourteen.

mt-19.title: Target 13: RBX1, with three structural zincs
mt-19.note: The clearest test of the cofactor rule: a RING domain coordinating three structural Zn2+, without which the fold does not exist. At least one ranking arm must represent them, and the count is asserted per scoring row. The native heteromeric Cullin-RING context is noted but not made part of the assay construct.

mt-20.title: Target 14: Nipah-G, monomeric head on a tetrameric virion
mt-20.note: The most conformationally ambiguous entry: a beta-propeller head that is monomeric in isolation but assembles into a stalk-mediated D2 homotetramer on the virion. Exactly the apo/holo and oligomer question the dossier rule exists to force a documented decision on.

mt-22.title: Reference access policy across targets
mt-22.note: Retains the single-target reference access policy, applying it across all fourteen targets. The 29-item reference list remains unshifted because the multi-target prompt does not prepend single-target competition links.

mt-54.title: Per-target dossier requirements
mt-54.note: Applies the dossier specification individually to each target. All mechanical constraints (frozen constructs, asserted chain and cofactor counts, and CONSTRUCT_FAIL handling) execute across all fourteen targets.

mt-129.title: Validation gate, plus a GDF-8 special case
mt-129.note: One sentence added: for GDF-8 specifically the gate file must additionally record a GDF-11 arm. The single-target GDF-8 prompts carry the equivalent clause phrased generally, because there the whole campaign is the selective one. Everything else about the gate is identical.

mt-135.title: Oligomer clause naming three targets
mt-135.note: The template slot filled with the multi-target set's actual oligomers: VEGF and GDF-8 homodimers, TNFα homotrimer. Eleven of the fourteen targets are monomers, so the 1:N and N:N double-scoring requirement binds on only three.

mt-145.title: Optimization depth allocated by difficulty
mt-145.note: Converts the uniform five-round minimum into a flexible floor: at least two rounds per target, extending to at least five on challenging targets. With 14 targets and a 5x budget increase, allocation is prioritized via target_weights.json.

mt-151.title: 30 designs per target
mt-151.note: The order grows from 30 to 420 designs by adding two words. Everything about how those 30 are selected, capped and ranked is unchanged.

mt-153.title: Compute economics, re-derived
mt-153.note: Same rate card, same formula, new arithmetic: $50,000 over 48 h is $1,042/h, roughly 237 H100-equivalents at even pace, so the 325-instance bootstrap cap runs 1.37x even pace rather than the single-target 1.58x. The multi-target campaign is proportionally more conservative at bootstrap.

mt-155.title: Governor parameters scaled for multi-target
mt-155.note: Scales numeric thresholds: concurrency ceiling to 325, bootstrap step to 50, and metered-versus-ratecard divergence limit to $200. All submit_gate conditions, timeout limits, and fail-closed behaviors remain identical. Typography matches the single-target prompt except for straight quotation marks in the cpu tag literal.

mt-161.title: Multi-target design volume
mt-161.note: Scales overall generation targets to 100,000 to 1,000,000 designs across the fourteen targets; per target, the expected volume falls by roughly a factor of three. The qualifier 'on a target' reframes the optimization trigger from campaign-wide to per-target.

mt-169.title: $50,000 of Modal spend
mt-169.note: Five times the single-target budget for fourteen times the targets, over twice the wall clock.

mt-174.title: Spend-to-target band at $50,000
mt-174.note: Same +/-10% band, same 'under-pace is a planning failure' framing. The list of ways to add work gains one option that only exists here: 'harder targets'.

mt-176.title: Multi-target scale-up triggers
mt-176.note: Enables scaling compute by allocating work toward more challenging targets alongside adding designs, seeds, or rounds. Target weighting logic operates across the complete fourteen-target panel.

mt-186.title: Kickoff post without a target in the header
mt-186.note: The header drops '(<target>)'. In the single-target release, concurrent campaigns against different targets share one Slack channel, so the target string is what disambiguates them; here there is one campaign covering all fourteen.

mt-187.title: Morning update across targets
mt-187.note: Omits single-target headers from morning updates while retaining all reporting obligations. Per-target gate statuses and progress metrics are reported within the update body.

mt-188.title: Hourly update reports per-target best scores
mt-188.note: Drops the single target name and asks instead for the current per-target best final_score. The hourly post becomes a fourteen-row summary rather than a one-line one.

mt-195.title: Campaign Drive folder structure
mt-195.note: Removes individual target names from the primary campaign folder. The single-writer invariant, close_out/ directory structure, and transactional snapshot procedures remain unchanged.

mt-224.title: Use the whole window
mt-224.note: Identical to the single-target block apart from a straight versus curly apostrophe. Recorded here because a naive byte diff of the two prompts reports it as a change; it is not one.

mt-226.title: Close-out reserve: three hours
mt-226.note: Tripled from one hour, and the surplus-plan trigger moves from more-than-2-hours-remaining to more-than-5. Fourteen sheets, fourteen supplements and a 420-row order take proportionally longer to freeze, verify and upload than one.

mt-230.title: 48 hours
mt-230.note: Double the single-target window, against fourteen times the targets. The mismatch between those two ratios is what forces most of the other scaling decisions in this document.

mt-232.title: Concurrency limits for 48-hour window
mt-232.note: Adjusts maximum limits for the expanded campaign: daemon ceiling rises to min(450, ...) and subagent headroom rises to 100. Timekeeping, dormancy tracking, and CLOCK singleton routines remain identical.

mt-234.title: Orchestrator initialization with 325 ceiling
mt-234.note: Initializes the governor with ceiling 325 and invokes set_concurrency_limit(325). Orchestrator discipline, prohibition of provider SDK calls, and blocking on SETUP remain unchanged.

mt-236.title: Plan for >100 concurrent agents
mt-236.note: Doubled from >50. The swarming architecture, the same-base-model requirement and the delegation-rejection fallback are otherwise unchanged.

mt-238.title: Delegation architecture with expanded headroom
mt-238.note: Increases subagent headroom from 50 to 100 while maintaining all watchdog escalation ladders, singleton liveness contracts, and dead-man fail-safes.

mt-254.title: Verification and roster PASS
mt-254.note: Identical to the single-target block apart from straight versus curly quotation marks around the 'metered unavailable' string. All five PASS conditions, the 10% budget cap per unvalidated model, the canary rule and the reap criterion are unchanged.

mt-268.title: Liveness, reaping, and the restart sequence
mt-268.note: One constant changed: the daemon concurrency ceiling in the restart sequence, min(200, ...) to min(450, ...), matching the raised governor. The single-reaper rule, the one-app rule and the five-step restart-from-durable-storage procedure are unchanged.

mt-278.title: Multi-target volume isolation
mt-278.note: Removes target identifiers from Modal volume names: campaign-<model>-<date>-<frameid8>-{state,ledger,out,novelty}. Four shared volumes support all fourteen targets, with records distinguished by internal target keys.
